guide.summary: OpenProject documents OAuth2 authorization code and client credentials flows. Each customer instance needs an OAuth application registered in its admin settings, then a user authorizes and the access token is sent as a Bearer token. The documented scope api_v3 is the default and the only scope named in the supplied passages; it is broader than read-only. Work package listing uses GET /api/v3/work_packages with offset and pageSize, and an empty filters array is needed to avoid a default filter. Test with one representative account on a test instance first. Whether the list endpoint requires view_work_packages, and the provider review and distribution model, remain unresolved.

findings.title: OAuth2 authorization code flow is documented
findings.detail: The provider documents an authorization URL and a token URL for the authorization code flow, with a consent prompt. This supports user-authorized access for the connected person.

evidence.quote: OAuth endpoints The authentication endpoints of OpenProject OAuth2 server are:

https://example.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<Client ID>&redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>&scope=<scope>&prompt=consent This requests redirects you to a URL that holds a code parameter which is the authentication code.

findings.title: OAuth application must be registered in each OpenProject instance
findings.detail: Registration occurs in the instance's OAuth application settings, which record a Client ID and Client secret. The redirect URL must match the client application. Each customer instance's registration is an administrator-owned step; the supplied sources do not establish how multi-instance registration is handled.

findings.title: Request the api_v3 scope for standard API access
findings.detail: If no scope is checked, the provider assumes api_v3, which is the standard API. The supplied passages do not document a narrower read-only OAuth scope, so the token's boundary is the whole standard API as limited by the user's own permissions.

steps.detail: Open the authorization URL on the test instance (replace the host with your instance host), signed in as the representative test user, and approve access. Capture the code value from the redirect.

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: Exchange the code at the instance token URL using the authorization_code grant. Keep the access token for the API test; do not reuse personal API tokens. Expected response includes access_token and expires_in.
steps.doneWhen: The token response contains an access_token value for the test account.

steps.title: Read first page of work packages
steps.detail: Send a GET request for page 1 with pageSize=20 and filters set to an empty array so no default filter applies. Expected response is a collection of work packages whose titles are visible. Boundary check: confirm that only GET is sent, no request body or write method is used, and that returned titles match work packages the test account can view in the instance UI.
steps.doneWhen: The response lists work package titles for the test account, and the request log shows only GET calls.

evidence.quote: get /api/v3/work_packages Returns a collection of work packages.
Parameters offset integer optional query
pageSize integer optional query
optional query JSON specifying filter conditions. Accepts the same format as returned by the queries endpoint. If no filter is to be applied, the client should send an empty array
$ curl --request GET 'https://example.com/api/v3/projects' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer <Token>' `

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash

steps.title: Check pagination continuation on the same endpoint
steps.detail: Repeat the same GET with offset=2 and the same pageSize and filters. Continue incrementing offset until a page returns no elements. The supplied sources do not document a total count or next link for this collection, so use the empty-page condition. Boundary check: confirm all requests remain GET and that no work package changes occur.
steps.doneWhen: Pages are read sequentially until an empty page, and all titles are recorded without any write request.
